# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Added opt-in OpenTelemetry request spans to both native hosts, off by default. `BRIDGE_OTEL_ENABLED=1` emits one `SERVER` span per request named `execute_tool <action>` (OpenTelemetry GenAI tool-execution convention) with `INTERNAL` child spans `bridge.policy_evaluate` and `bridge.extension_forward`; `BRIDGE_OTEL_ENDPOINT` posts OTLP/HTTP JSON to a collector, `BRIDGE_OTEL_FILE` appends the same document to a local file, and `BRIDGE_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` (default `chrome-bridge`) sets `service.name`. With `BRIDGE_OTEL_ENABLED` unset the path is inert in both hosts - no extra module import, no file, no socket - and request handling plus the response shape are identical to a host with no telemetry code. No `opentelemetry` SDK is required or used: the document written or posted is the OTLP/HTTP JSON wire format, built with the standard library in Python and `serde_json` in Rust. This is process-level configuration rather than policy, deliberately with no policy key, so tracing can never be enabled per client and can never change a policy decision.
- Span attributes are host-side metadata only: `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.type`, `bridge.action`, `bridge.client`, `bridge.decision`, `bridge.effective_tier` (from `effective_action_tier`), `bridge.duration_ms`, `bridge.tab_id_count`, `bridge.success`, `bridge.request_id`, `bridge.trace_id`, and `bridge.host`. No payload or any field of one (no selectors, no URLs, no typed text), no response body, no page content or snapshot, no cookies, no storage values, no bridge or confirmation tokens, and no credential values are ever attached; denial reasons and extension error strings are excluded too, since they can quote caller- or page-supplied text. The only attribute value not generated by the host is the caller's own trace/session id, and every string attribute is passed through the same `secretMaskFile` masking as the audit log before export. Nothing leaves the machine unless `BRIDGE_OTEL_ENDPOINT` is set. Export is best effort like an audit-log write: the OTLP POST runs on a background thread behind a bounded queue with a short timeout, and a failing sink is logged once and disabled, so telemetry can neither delay nor fail a browser request.
- Added W3C trace-context propagation. A `traceparent` field on the TCP request envelope, the incoming `traceparent` header on the MCP HTTP transport (read next to the per-request bridge token), a root trace minted per MCP stdio tool call when telemetry is enabled, and the new global CLI flag `chrome-bridge --traceparent <value>` all continue the caller's trace instead of starting a new one. Like the token and `dryRun`, `traceparent` is host-only and stripped before anything is forwarded to the extension; a malformed value starts a fresh trace rather than failing the request. When policy also sets `traceDir`, each session trace event additionally carries `otelTraceId` and `otelSpanId` alongside its existing `traceId`, so a local JSONL artifact and an exported span describe the same request; with telemetry disabled those fields are absent and the artifact is unchanged. The Rust host emits the identical span model, attribute keys, and OTLP document, but its exporter is a minimal `std::net` HTTP/1.1 writer, so `BRIDGE_OTEL_ENDPOINT` must be a cleartext `http://` collector (an `https://` endpoint is refused with one log line instead of linking a TLS stack into the host); `BRIDGE_OTEL_FILE` behaves identically on both hosts.
- Added credential handoff scoped to one field: extension action `credentialHandoff` `{tabId?, selector, message?, mode?, timeoutMs?}`, CLI `chrome-bridge credentialHandoff <tabId> <selector> [message] [--mode filled|submitted] [--timeout <ms>]`, and MCP `browser_credential_handoff` (mutating, not sensitive). This is now the supported way to get a password, passphrase, recovery code, or one-time code into a page, replacing any use of `fill` for a secret: the agent supplies a selector, never a value. The selector resolves through the normal locator grammar (CSS, `text=`/`label=`/`role=`/`aria=`, `shadow >>>`, `ref=eN`; frame-scoped selectors are rejected), every capture buffer for the tab is dropped **before** anything is focused, and the field is then polled through an injected check that returns only `{present, empty, length}` - the value is never read, echoed, hashed, logged, or traced anywhere in the path. A success response carries identity only: `{success, tabId, selector, mode, filled, valueLength, elapsedMs, scrubbedCaptures}`, where `valueLength` is a character count so a caller can confirm something was entered. `mode` is `filled` (default; resolves once the field goes from empty to non-empty and the length settles) or `submitted` (resolves on form submit or navigation); `timeoutMs` defaults to 120000 and a timeout returns `credential handoff timeout after <n>ms`. Both native hosts register `credentialHandoff` in the same in-flight handoff registry as `waitForHandoff`, with identical scoping (numeric `tabId` scopes to that tab, no `tabId` is global, and an observation with no `tabId` is denied by any live handoff), the same `handoff in progress` error, the same `handoff_blackout` audit decision, and release in a `finally` on success, error, and timeout. It is deliberately **not** in the example policy's `requireConfirmation`: gating the safe path would push callers back toward typing secrets through `fill`.
- Read-only versus state-changing classification is now computed from the payload rather than the action name alone, in both native hosts. `effective_action_tier(action, payload)` resolves `read_only` or `mutating` from a single data-driven escalation table (`ESCALATING_PAYLOAD_FLAGS`, identical in `bridge.py` and `host-rs/src/main.rs`): `screencastFrames` escalates unless `consume` is literally `false`, because the default drains the frame buffer irrecoverably; `cacheSelectors` escalates on `op` of `clear` or `import`; `resolveCachedSelector` escalates when `cache` carries a non-empty array of entries to merge. A `batch` or `replayWorkflow` is the union over its steps - `read_only` only when every step is, mutating as soon as one step is - reusing the same step extraction (and `tabId` defaulting/retargeting) the policy walk already applies. That effective tier, not the action name, now drives the `siteModes` `manual` gate, so an all-read-only batch is no longer force-gated while one carrying a single mutating step is; the `manual` gate additionally resolves a batch's mode from the union of its steps' live origins, closing a bypass where hoisting mutating actions into an origin-exempt `batch` dodged a manual origin. `skip` can never waive a confirmation for a payload-escalated call. Every `policyCheck` verdict (single and per plan step) and every dry-run verdict now reports `effectiveTier`. `consoleMessages`, `networkRequests`, `interceptedRequests`, `observe`, `getCurrentState`, and `searchTabs` were audited and stay read-only for every payload they accept. MCP annotations are static per tool and stay conservative - `browser_batch` and `browser_screencast_save` remain annotated mutating - with the host-side tier documented as authoritative.
- Added deterministic postconditions: extension action `expect`, CLI `chrome-bridge expect <tabId> selector|text|url|schema <value> [--negate] [--timeout <ms>]`, and MCP `browser_expect` (read-only). `expect` answers one closed question with no model in the path: `selector` passes when the selector resolves through the normal locator grammar (CSS, `text=`/`label=`/`role=`/`aria=`, `frame=`, `shadow >>>`, `ref=eN`), `text` when the page text contains the string, `url` when the tab URL contains the substring, and `schema` when structured extraction against the schema reports no `missingRequired` errors, reusing `extractStructured` rather than duplicating extraction. `negate` inverts the outcome so absence can be asserted, and the check polls every 250 ms until the condition holds or `timeoutMs` (default 5000, capped at 60000) elapses. It is an assertion, not a read: the response carries `mode`, `negate`, `passed`, `attempts`, `elapsedMs`, and a short `reason` only when it failed - never the matched element, the matched text, the tab URL, or the extracted values - and the CLI exits `1` when the assertion did not hold so it composes in shell scripts and CI.
- Extended replayable workflows to version 2 with per-step postconditions and bounded retry. A step may carry `expect` (the `expect` payload shape minus `tabId`) and `retry` `{max, delayMs}` with `max` clamped `0..5` and `delayMs` clamped `0..10000`; out-of-range or malformed values clamp instead of rejecting the file. The postcondition is evaluated after the step's own action succeeds, and a failure re-runs the whole step - dispatch plus assertion - up to `retry.max` times with `retry.delayMs` between attempts before failing it with `{"success": false, "err": "expect failed", "step": <index>, "action": ..., "expect": {"mode": ..., "reason": ...}}` under the usual `stopOnError` semantics. Each step in the replay result now reports `attempts`, `retried`, and (with a postcondition) `expectPassed`, plus `retriedSteps`/`expectFailedSteps` totals and the file's own `workflowVersion`, so the artifact is evidence rather than a self-assessment. Both hosts enumerate a step's `expect` clause as a nested read-only `expect` step, so a postcondition is origin-checked like any other tab-scoped action. Version-1 files have neither key and replay byte-for-byte unchanged; recording never invents an `expect` clause.
- Added record-and-replay macros: extension actions `startWorkflowRecording`, `stopWorkflowRecording`, `replayWorkflow`, CLI `chrome-bridge workflow record start|stop|save` and `chrome-bridge workflow replay <path> [--tab <tabId>] [--binding key=value] [--continue-on-error]`, and MCP `browser_replay_workflow`. A recording captures **only what the bridge dispatched** - every mutating action that returns successfully through the extension's dispatch table, never a human click or keystroke, and never a failed action - so it can reproduce nothing the recording client was not already allowed to do. Recordings live in service-worker memory (dropped on a worker restart, capped at 500 steps) and are scoped to one tab with `--tab` or global, with profile-wide steps such as `setCookie` recorded either way. `stop` serializes to the shared workflow contract `{version: 2, name, createdAt, steps: [{action, payload, wait?}], policy: {requiredOrigins}}` - the same format `chrome-bridge schedule` validates - where `wait` is the recorded inter-step gap clamped to 10000 ms and `requiredOrigins` collects every origin the recording touched. Typed and stored values are redacted by default: `type`/`fill` text, `setCookie`/`setStorageItem` values, `handleDialog` prompt text, and any credential-shaped payload key become `<redacted>` with `requiresValue: true` and a `bindingKeys` entry such as `step3.text`, and replay refuses the **entire** workflow before running any step until every one is supplied through `--binding`/`bindings`; `--record-sensitive` (or `recordSensitive: true` on one call) opts out and writes the literal value into the file. Both native hosts police `replayWorkflow` step by step **before the outer request is forwarded at all**: they walk `workflow.steps[]`, apply the same `--tab` retargeting the extension will apply, and run each step through the action, origin, `siteModes`, lease, and blackout gates. Any denied step denies the whole replay as `policy denied: workflow step <n>: <reason>` (with the index in `policyDenial.batchStep`), and a reserved host-internal action can never be dispatched as a step. There is no aggregate confirmation token: a nested step that still requires confirmation fails the replay as `policy denied: workflow step <n> requires confirmation` and mints nothing, so grant that step through policy or a `skip` site mode. The extension additionally refuses any step whose live tab origin is not in `requiredOrigins`. `stop`/`save` write the workflow to git-ignored `bridge_workflow_last.json` and any `--out`/`save` path at mode `600` and print metadata only; `startWorkflowRecording` and `replayWorkflow` are confirmation-gated in the example policy.
- Added an action cache with selector self-healing: extension actions `resolveCachedSelector` and `cacheSelectors`, CLI `chrome-bridge cache selectors list [--sync] | clear [--local-only] | export <path> | import <path>`, and MCP `browser_cache_selectors` / `browser_resolve_cached_selector`. For `click`, `type`, `fill`, `select`, and `hover`, a semantic selector (`text=`, `label=`, `role=`, `aria=`) is resolved once and the concrete document-unique CSS path it landed on - id, then `data-testid`/`data-test-id`/`data-test`/`name`/`aria-label`, then an `nth-of-type` path anchored at the nearest such attribute - is cached against `(origin + pathname, selector)`; `resolveCachedSelector` also mints an observe-compatible `ref=eN` for the resolved element. Replay uses the cached path first and, when it no longer resolves, re-resolves the original semantic selector, rewrites the cache, and reports `selfHealed: true` on the step. A **CSS selector is never cached and never retargeted** - a stale CSS step fails rather than acting on a different element - and frame- or shadow-scoped selectors resolve but report `cacheable: false` because their path is relative to another document. The file-backed copy lives in git-ignored `bridge_action_cache.json` (mode `600`); imported entries whose selector is not semantic are rejected and counted, in both the CLI and the extension.
- Added per-site permission modes to both native hosts through the new policy key `siteModes`, a map of origin pattern to `manual`, `auto`, or `skip`. It is merged per pattern across the `default` and `clients.<name>` layers, so a client override of one origin inherits every other origin's mode. `manual` requires a confirmation token for every mutating or high-risk action on a matching origin even when `requireConfirmation` is empty; `auto` is the existing behavior; `skip` pre-approves the confirmation gate so no token is minted, and the waiver is audited as decision `confirmation_waived` with reason `siteMode skip`. Modes move only the confirmation gate: a `deniedActions`/`deniedOrigins` match still denies, and `skip` can never waive `executeScript`, `executeScriptCDP`, `getCookies`, `storageState`, `setCookie`, `deleteCookie`, `setStorageItem`, `removeStorageItem`, `clearStorage`, `startScreencast`, or `clickAt`. Overlapping patterns resolve identically in both hosts (longest pattern wins, ties broken lexicographically), an unknown mode value is ignored rather than guessed at, and a configured `siteModes` map now also makes tab-scoped requests resolve their live origin. `policyCheck`, `policyCheck --plan`, and `dryRun` verdicts gained a `siteMode` field. Edit modes with `chrome-bridge policy site-mode <originPattern> manual|auto|skip [client]` and `chrome-bridge policy clear-site-mode <originPattern> [client]`; MCP exposes no policy-mutation tool by design.
- Added scheduled-workflow registration: `chrome-bridge schedule workflow <workflowPath> --at <ISO8601>|--interval <seconds> [--name <name>]`, `chrome-bridge schedule list`, and `chrome-bridge schedule remove <name>`. This registers **metadata only** into git-ignored `bridge_schedules.json` (mode `600`, overridable with `BRIDGE_SCHEDULE_FILE`) and deliberately ships **no daemon and no timer**: nothing runs until cron, launchd, systemd, a CI job, or a human invokes the printed `runCommand`, and every response says so with `runsUnattended: false`. Registration authorizes nothing - the host still evaluates each replayed step against the live policy. The workflow file contract `{version, name, steps: [{action, payload?, wait?}], policy: {requiredOrigins?}}` is validated before an entry is written (`--interval` under 60 seconds is rejected, re-registering a name replaces it), and an entry records only the name, workflow path, trigger, step count, declared required origins, registration time, and run command - never a step payload.
- Added schema-driven extraction: extension action `extractStructured`, CLI `chrome-bridge extractStructured <tabId> <schemaPath> [outputPath] [--selector <selector>] [--max-chars <count>]`, and MCP `browser_extract_structured`. The schema is a JSON Schema subset (`object`, `array`, `string`, `number`, `boolean`, plus `enum`, `required`, `properties`, `items`) and anything outside it is rejected up front rather than ignored. Mapping is deterministic and heuristic with no model inference: field names and their de-camel-cased forms are matched against `dl` term/definition pairs, single-value table rows, form-control labels, `aria-label`, `itemprop`/`data-field`, `name` attributes, headings followed by a value block, and `Key: value` text lines; arrays of objects come from a table whose headers match the item properties, arrays of scalars from a labelled list or a delimited value. Fields with no confident value are omitted rather than guessed, missing required fields are reported in `errors` with a `path` and a `code`, and the extracted data is re-validated against the schema before it is returned alongside `schemaVersion`. Raw page text never leaves the extension; with `outputPath` the data is written to that file and stdout carries metadata only.
- Added a prompt-injection posture scan: extension action `scanPromptInjection`, CLI `chrome-bridge scanPromptInjection <tabId> [--selector <selector>] [--max-chars <count>]`, MCP `browser_scan_prompt_injection`, and an opt-in `scanPromptInjection: true` payload flag on `extractText`/`getHTML` (MCP `browser_extract_text(scan_prompt_injection=True)`) that adds the same report as an `injectionScan` field without changing their existing result shape. The scan flags instruction-like page text by kind - instruction override, system-prompt disclosure, credential exfiltration, shell execution, policy tampering, operator concealment, permission coercion, tool redirection, URL-borne data exfiltration - and returns `risk` (`low`/`medium`/`high`), `matches` with `kind`, `severity`, and a snippet capped at 160 characters, and `scannedChars`. Full page text is never returned. The scanner is heuristic: `docs/security.md` documents that page content stays untrusted data and that a scan result is never a permission grant or denial, with policy, confirmation gates, the origin allowlist, and the handoff blackout remaining the only enforcement surface.
- Added Windows support: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup-windows.ps1` registers the native host for the current user only. It accepts `-RepoRoot`, `-HostPort` (default 9223), `-ExtensionId`, `-UseRustHost`, and `-Browser Chrome|Edge|Both`, writes the git-ignored `bridge-host-launch.cmd` launcher (Windows native messaging launches the manifest path directly, so the interpreter lives in a wrapper) for either `python.exe bridge.py` or `host-rs\target\release\bridge-host.exe`, generates `com.automation.bridge.json`, and writes the manifest path to the **unnamed default value** of `HKCU:\Software\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts\com.automation.bridge` (plus the matching Edge key when asked) with `Set-Item`, then reads it back and throws if it did not take. `Set-ItemProperty -Name "(Default)"` cannot write that value - it creates a separate value literally named `(Default)` and leaves the real default empty, so the browser finds no host - and `verify_install_contract.py` now rejects that pattern statically. It writes no `HKLM` key and needs no elevation, creates `bridge_token.txt`, `bridge_tokens.txt`, and `bridge_policy.json` only when absent while restricting each to the current user with `icacls`, and prints metadata only - manifest path, host name, host kind, port, extension ID, and next steps - never a token value.
- Added Microsoft Edge support: `./setup-edge.sh` adds an Edge registration to an existing macOS/Linux install. Edge is Chromium, so the canonical extension is used unchanged; the script creates no secrets, resolves the extension ID and host path from the existing setup output (or `--extension-id`/`--host-path`), regenerates the Edge manifest, and symlinks it into the Edge, Beta, Dev, and Canary native-messaging directories. On Windows use `setup-windows.ps1 -Browser Edge`.
- Added `scripts/generate_browser_manifests.py`, a deterministic generator for Edge and Firefox native-messaging artifacts under the git-ignored `dist/browsers`. Firefox output is a host manifest using `allowed_extensions` plus a staged extension directory whose manifest is the canonical manifest with only the Gecko differences applied: `browser_specific_settings.gecko.id`, `background: {"scripts": ["background.js"]}` instead of a service worker, and the Chrome-only permissions `debugger`, `tabGroups`, and `contentSettings` dropped and reported. The canonical Chrome manifest is untouched, nothing is registered, no secret is read, and stdout is metadata only. Firefox is explicitly an unsupported runtime: without `chrome.debugger` there is no background-safe screenshot, `printToPDF`, `clickAt`, screencast, `executeScriptCDP`, performance metrics, throttling, or emulation, and no live gate in this repository exercises it.
- Extended `verify_install_contract.py` with cross-platform install coverage: static shape checks for `setup-windows.ps1` (HKCU-only registry strings, no `HKLM:`/elevation, required parameters, git-ignored `.cmd` launcher, secrets kept rather than overwritten, no statement that can print the token, balanced delimiters) and `setup-edge.sh`, plus a real temp-directory run of the browser-manifest generator asserting the exact Edge and Firefox manifest objects, the exact staging file set with no forbidden artifact, byte-identical copied files, the staged manifest differences, digest determinism across two runs, and rejection of bad extension IDs, add-on IDs, and relative host paths.
- Added source-mapped console stacks. Every `consoleMessages` entry now carries a `stack` of the raw generated frames CDP reported (`url`, 0-based `lineNumber`/`columnNumber`, `functionName`, `scriptId`); log entries with no stack fall back to a single frame built from the entry's own url and line. The new optional payload `resolveSourceMaps: true` (CLI `chrome-bridge consoleMessages <tabId> --source-maps`, MCP `browser_console_messages(tab_id, resolve_source_maps=True)`) adds best-effort resolution: the extension reads each script through CDP `Debugger.getScriptSource` (falling back to a plain fetch), parses a trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment, and decodes source-map v3 with a dependency-free VLQ decoder in the service worker, adding `originalLocation` (`source`, `name`, 0-based `lineNumber`/`columnNumber`) or a `sourceMapStatus` of `notFound`, `invalid`, `unmapped`, or `crossOriginRefused`. Only the script's own origin or an inline `data:application/json` map is read, so no third-party origin is contacted; script text and the map's `sourcesContent` are never retained or returned, and the CLI scrubs source-text-shaped fields before printing. Parsed maps are cached in service-worker memory per tab and script URL, capped at 100 entries and dropped when the tab closes. The default response shape is unchanged.
- Added `scripts/package_extension_store.py`, a store-ready extension packaging path: `python3 scripts/package_extension_store.py --out dist/chrome-bridge-extension-store.zip [--check-js]` writes a zip containing exactly `manifest.json`, `background.js`, `wake.html`, and `wake.js` and prints metadata only (path, sha256, byte count, per-file list). Entries are written sorted with a fixed timestamp, so unchanged inputs produce an identical digest. Before writing, the script fails closed on a drifted `extension/` mirror, a non-MV3 manifest, a manifest that drops any canonical root permission or carries a `key` (checked against the manifest as read from disk, before the packager touches it, so a key is a hard failure rather than a silent strip), a `background.js` that does not reference the `com.automation.bridge` native host, or any forbidden local artifact name. `--check-js` runs `node --check` and is off by default. The script never creates, reads, or packages `extension_key.pem`, never uploads, and never calls a Chrome Web Store API; `verify_install_contract.py` now covers the member set, forbidden-pattern absence, digest determinism, rejection of a manifest missing root permissions, and rejection of a staged `--source` manifest carrying a `key` with no archive written.
- Added session trace artifacts behind the new optional policy key `traceDir`. Both hosts append exactly one JSONL event per trace-eligible request to `<traceDir>/<traceId>.jsonl` once the request is fully processed - allow, host denial, extension error, or timeout. A request is eligible when its payload carries `sessionId`, `taskSessionId`, or an explicit `traceId`, when the action is `createTaskSession`/`navigateTaskSession`/`closeTaskSession`, or when the response result carries a `sessionId`; the trace id follows that same priority and the file name is sanitized to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` and capped at 80 characters. Each event records `ts`, `client`, `action`, `decision`, `reason`, `requestId`, `durationMs`, `targets` (tab ids only), `traceId`, `responseHash` (SHA-256 of the canonical redacted response), `snapshotHash` when the response carried an observe snapshot or diff, and `success` - never a payload body, a response body, or a token, with secret masking applied before hashing. Read artifacts with `chrome-bridge trace summary <traceId>` / `chrome-bridge trace tail <traceId> [count]` (both accept `--trace-dir`) or MCP `browser_trace_summary` / `browser_trace_tail`; `policyInfo` now reports the active `traceDir`, and `bridge_traces/` is git-ignored.
- Added stable element refs to `observe`: every node now carries a `ref` such as `e12`, and `ref=e12` is a first-class selector prefix accepted wherever a selector is (`click`, `type`, `fill`, `hover`, `drag`, `select`, `uploadFile`, `scroll`, `waitForSelector`, and the matching MCP tools). A ref resolves through the live CDP node recorded at snapshot time, not by re-matching text, so it addresses the exact element that was observed. Refs are minted per tab in extension service-worker memory with a counter that never rewinds; a navigation or a worker restart invalidates them, and an unknown or invalidated ref fails with `{"success": false, "error": "staleRef", "hint": "re-run observe"}` instead of silently falling back to CSS matching.
- Added `observe` snapshot diffing: `chrome-bridge observe <tabId> --diff` (payload `diff: true`, MCP `browser_snapshot(diff=True)`) returns `added` nodes, `removed` refs, and `changed` nodes whose role, name, or value moved, plus `baseEpoch` and `epoch` identifying the two snapshots. Only the latest snapshot is retained per tab, capped at 5000 nodes; the first diff call with no baseline returns the full snapshot with `diffBase: true`.
- Added screencast recording: extension actions `startScreencast`, `screencastFrames`, `stopScreencast`, CLI `chrome-bridge startScreencast <tabId> [--quality N] [--max-width N]`, `chrome-bridge screencastSave <tabId> <outputDir> [--fps 8] [--mp4]`, `chrome-bridge stopScreencast <tabId>`, and MCP `browser_start_screencast`, `browser_stop_screencast`, `browser_screencast_save`. Capture runs on the same background-safe debugger path as `screenshot`, so a background tab is never activated. Frames are acknowledged per CDP requirement and buffered only in the extension service worker (memory-only: a worker restart ends the recording) with a hard bound of 600 frames or ~50MB, dropping the oldest frames and reporting `droppedFrames`. `screencastSave` writes numbered frame files plus a `frames.json` manifest and prints only directory, counts, and byte totals; `--mp4` assembles `screencast.mp4` with the system `ffmpeg` when present and otherwise keeps the frames with an explicit note. `startScreencast` ships confirmation-gated in the sample policy because continuous capture of a real profile is high-exposure.
- Added a handoff telemetry blackout to both native hosts: while a `waitForHandoff` request is in flight, the one-shot observations `screenshot`, `extractText`, `getHTML`, `storageState`, `printToPDF`, `searchTabs`, `getCurrentState`, `extractStructured`, `scanPromptInjection`, and `observe`, the collector reads `consoleMessages`, `networkRequests`, `interceptedRequests`, and `screencastFrames`, and the collector starts `startMonitoring`, `startInterception`, and `startScreencast` are denied before policy evaluation with `{"success": false, "error": "handoff in progress", "blackout": true}` and audited as `handoff_blackout`, so no client - including the one that requested the handoff - can observe a human typing credentials. The blackout is scoped to the handoff's `tabId` and covers every tab when the handoff has none; `dryRun` reports it in the verdict; the in-flight record is released on every exit path. A `batch` or `replayWorkflow` wrapping a blacked-out step is denied as a whole, since those steps are dispatched inside the extension and would never reach the gate individually. Both hosts load every configured `secretMaskFile` on the initial policy load, before the socket server accepts a connection, so even a first-request denial that quotes a secret in its target is audited masked.
- Added per-request bridge tokens to the MCP HTTP transport. Under `BRIDGE_MCP_TRANSPORT=http` each request may carry `Authorization: Bearer <bridge-token>` (or `X-Bridge-Token: <token>` as a fallback; Bearer wins), which is used as that request's host identity instead of the server's ambient `bridge_token.txt`. Several agents can now share one HTTP endpoint and still get their own policy scoping, audit attribution, and cooperative lease arbitration. No header keeps the previous ambient behavior, stdio is unchanged, and token values are never logged or echoed in errors. The process-wide automatic lease wrapper is disabled under HTTP (its cached state assumes one identity per process); HTTP clients call `browser_lease`/`browser_release` explicitly.
- Documented parallel work under one token in `docs/multi-agent.md`: the lease arbitrates between token identities only, so concurrent task sessions (one per workstream, inactive tabs, lease taken only around mutating bursts) are the supported intra-token concurrency pattern.
- Added `chrome-bridge policyCheck --plan '<jsonArray>'` and MCP `browser_plan_preview` to preflight up to 50 `{action, origin, payload}` steps in one host-side call, returning a per-step verdict (`step`, `action`, `allowed`, `reason`, `confirmationRequired`, `redact`, `audit`, `originDependent`). Nothing is forwarded to Chrome.
- Added a request-level dry run: global CLI `--dry-run`, or `"dryRun": true` in an MCP `browser_action` payload. Both hosts run the full pipeline - token check, policy evaluation, lease check, origin-dependency determination - then stop before forwarding and return `{success, dryRun, wouldForward, action, targets, verdict}`. Confirmation-gated actions report `confirmationRequired` without minting a token, and no lease, approval prompt, or live-origin lookup is triggered.
- Added the optional policy key `secretMaskFile`, a local `name=value` file (see `bridge_secrets.txt.example`) whose values both hosts replace with `<masked:name>` in every outbound response string and every audit-log field, independently of the `redact` toggle. A missing file disables masking for that path after one warning recorded as `secret_mask_unavailable`.
- Added cookie and web-storage write ops - `chrome-bridge setCookie`, `deleteCookie`, `setStorageItem`, `removeStorageItem`, `clearStorage` and MCP `browser_set_cookie`, `browser_delete_cookie`, `browser_set_storage_item`, `browser_remove_storage_item`, `browser_clear_storage`. All five are confirmation-gated in the sample policy, sit behind `BRIDGE_MCP_ALLOW_SENSITIVE` on MCP, and never log or echo the written value: responses carry cookie name and domain, storage scope and key, or removed key counts only.
- Added `chrome-bridge searchHistory <query> [maxResults] [--since <epochMillis>]` and `chrome-bridge searchBookmarks <query>` plus MCP `browser_search_history` and `browser_search_bookmarks`, using the new `history` and `bookmarks` extension permissions. Both read the real profile's private browsing record, so they are confirmation-gated in the sample policy, sensitive-tier on MCP, and listed under raw-output safety.
- Added `chrome-bridge searchTabs <query> [--regex] [--max-per-tab <count>] [--case-sensitive]` and MCP `browser_search_tabs` to find text across every open http/https tab. Results report tab id, origin host (never the full URL), match count, and capped snippets of the match plus 80 characters of context; unscriptable tabs are skipped and only counted.
- Added `chrome-bridge printToPDF <tabId> <outputPath> [--landscape] [--scale <factor>]` and MCP `browser_save_pdf`, exporting a tab through CDP `Page.printToPDF` on the same background-safe debugger path as `screenshot`; the CLI writes the PDF and prints path, MIME type, and byte count only.
- Added `chrome-bridge clickAt <tabId> <x> <y>` and MCP `browser_click_at` for coordinate clicks on canvas/map/PDF surfaces no selector can reach. Because no element is resolved there is nothing to audit, so `clickAt` ships confirmation-gated in the sample policy.
- Added `chrome-bridge windowControl list|create|focus|setState|close` and MCP `browser_window_control`. `list` reports only window id, focus, state, type, and tab count - never tab URLs or titles; `create` opens unfocused by default; `close` refuses to close the last remaining normal browser window.
- Extended `batch` with a per-step `timeoutMs` passthrough and a per-batch `stopOnError` (default `true`, `--continue-on-error` on the CLI) that records failed steps in place instead of aborting. Wait actions already interleaved with mutating steps through the shared dispatch table; that behavior is now documented precisely.
- Added `chrome-bridge audit tail [count]` and `chrome-bridge audit summary [--since <ISO8601|7d|12h|30m>]` to read the local audit log: recent decisions as aligned columns and aggregate per-client/per-action/outcome counts with the top deny reasons. Metadata only, never payloads; malformed lines are counted, and a missing log or unreachable host is reported explicitly.
- Added `scripts/quick_install.sh`, a one-command bootstrap that runs `./setup.sh` (with optional port passthrough), probes the bridge, and prints the unpacked-extension directory, `chrome://extensions/` steps, and a ready-to-paste MCP registration block for the current checkout.
- Fixed packaged MCP startup so repo-local CLI helpers load without a manual `PYTHONPATH`, and added one safe reconnect attempt when TCP connection setup fails before an action is sent.
- Added token-only confirmation resume through `chrome-bridge confirm <token>` and MCP `browser_confirm`; confirmation responses now include the exact resume command.
- Added `chrome-bridge github-attach-pr-body <tabId> <files...>` and MCP `browser_github_attach_pr_body` to open a PR body editor, upload through GitHub's attachment component, wait for CDN links, and save.
- Added normal top-level/per-command CLI help, compact and filtered `observe`, and `aria=<accessible-name>` selectors alongside existing `text=`, `label=`, and `role=` selectors.
- Added durable task sessions with owned tabs, named Chrome tab groups, safe session cleanup, CLI commands, and typed MCP tools.
- Added a machine-readable background reliability harness that detects active-tab changes, frontmost-app changes, unexpected tabs, and owned tabs becoming active.
- Routine CLI and broker retries no longer open a visible extension wake tab when the native backend is unavailable.
- Navigation now opens inactive tabs by default; pass `--foreground` for an intentional user-visible tab.
- Screenshots now use the background-safe debugger path by default; pass `--visible` for an intentional visible-tab capture.
- Added `scripts/diagnose_install.py` to report deployed-file drift and broker/backend connection state without waking Chrome.
- Hardened selector-cache retargeting: a cache hit is now trusted only when the cached CSS path and the original semantic selector resolve to the **same live DOM node** (compared by CDP backend node id). A cached path that still resolves but now addresses a replacement element is discarded exactly like one that stopped resolving - the semantic selector is re-resolved, the cache is rewritten, and the step reports `selfHealed: true` - so replay acts on the target the author named instead of whatever the stale path happens to match. Imported cache entries are validated the same way at resolution time.
- Fixed source-map resolution fabricating positions: a generated column left of the first mapping segment on its line now reports `sourceMapStatus: "unmapped"` instead of borrowing that segment's original location.
- Reclassified two MCP tools that were exposed as read-only. `browser_search_tabs` is now sensitive (it returns snippets from every open tab of the real profile) and requires `BRIDGE_MCP_ALLOW_SENSITIVE=1`; `browser_screencast_save` (consumes the extension frame buffer, writes local files) and `browser_cache_selectors` (supports `clear`/`import`) are now classified mutating, annotated `readOnlyHint: false`/`destructiveHint: true`, and dropped under `BRIDGE_MCP_READONLY=1`.
- Fixed screencast saves mixing recordings and losing frames. `chrome-bridge screencastSave` and MCP `browser_screencast_save` now create and validate the destination **before** draining the extension's buffer - draining is irrecoverable, so an unwritable destination fails while the frames are still there - and clear only a prior save's artifacts (`frame-*.png`, `frame-*.jpg`, `frames.json`, `screencast.mp4`) so a shorter second save cannot present an earlier recording's tail as its own. The manifest is written to a temp file and renamed, and both report `staleArtifactsRemoved`.
- The extension now stops capturing the handoff tab. `waitForHandoff` scrubs that tab's monitor buffers (console, network, dialogs), intercepted-request buffer, and screencast frames and stops those surfaces before showing the banner, reporting the result in `scrubbedCaptures`. Buffers are dropped before any CDP round trip, so a tab that refuses the stop commands still retains nothing - the host-side blackout refuses reads, but only this prevents a buffer filled during the handoff from being drained afterward.

All notable user-facing changes for Chrome Native Messaging Automation Bridge are recorded here.

## 1.0.1 - Public release candidate

### Security and trust model

- Added recursive host-side redaction for sensitive results returned through `batch`, matching standalone action redaction for cookies, storage state, HTML/text extraction, and script results across the Python and Rust hosts.
- Kept `executeScriptCDP` out of the sample policy's default allowed actions; users must opt into high-risk debugger/script capabilities deliberately.
- Clarified that same-channel confirmation is accidental-use friction for trusted token holders, not protection from a compromised bridge token.
- Documented the trusted-local security model earlier in the README.

### Release packaging

- Source release archives are built from tracked files only, so ignored or untracked local artifacts do not leak into public zips.
- The unpacked extension artifact now contains the complete developer-mode extension surface: `background.js`, `manifest.json`, `wake.html`, and `wake.js`.
- Local policy backups, tokens, generated manifests, virtualenvs, lockfiles, debug logs, audit logs, and WIP patches are excluded from release artifacts.

### Installation and workflows

- CI and release workflows now run the same core gate set, including broker, GitHub attachment, install, live-smoke, Rust parity, guardrail, lease, and benchmark contract checks.
- `setup.sh` and `setup-rs.sh` no longer imply that an unpacked extension was deployed when `--extension-id` registers a packaged or store-managed extension ID.
- `setup-broker.sh` now prints the state-dir extension path and token-file advice after a successful broker setup.
- Live install smoke now passes the selected host port through setup and verifies the reported setup JSON shape.

### Documentation

- Removed stale static benchmark timing tables and replaced them with instructions for generating fresh local reports.
- Narrowed platform-support language to documented macOS/Linux installer paths.
- Clarified broker-mode state directory identity, MCP versioning, local usage diagnostics, and release artifact boundaries.

### Excluded from this release

- XChat response-capture work is intentionally not included in this public release candidate. The local WIP was preserved outside Git under `.wip/` for a future hardening pass.
